note: Authoritative local data from L1 chains.db (DeFiLlama + CoinGecko + growthepie/Dune). Raw signals, no scores. null = NO DATA (do not guess). FRESHNESS: price & market caps are live (today); TVL/stablecoin LEVELS are the latest available (carried forward if a chain's today-point isn't in yet); daily-FLOW metrics (DEX volume, fees, active_addresses, tx_count) are the LAST COMPLETE UTC DAY (today is partial and excluded) — full-day figures, use them as-is. SHARES are each chain's % of the WHOLE DeFi market (all ~500 chains; denominators in market.total_*), so tracked chains sum to <100% and deltas are immune to which chains we track. TVL/volume are USD-denominated, so share moves in a big market swing partly reflect token price, not pure flows. Each chain ALSO carries its OWN raw TVL growth — tvl_change_1d/7d/30d_pct (chain's level vs itself N days ago); use THESE for 'is this chain's TVL growing', NOT the share deltas (share = slice of market, a different question). If tvl_suspect_1d is true the 1d move is a likely upstream data glitch (a >25% one-day swing) — discount the 1d figure and lean on the 7d/30d trend instead. Stablecoins mirror this: stable_change_1d/7d/30d_pct are the chain's OWN stablecoin-supply trend (use for 'is stablecoin capital arriving/leaving', and to confirm or debunk 'stables doubled/halved' claims); stable_suspect_1d flags a >30% one-day swing as a likely DeFiLlama adapter flap (a bridged asset dropping in/out of the index) — call it out as a data-quality event, not a capital flow, and lean on 7d/30d. N-days-ago baselines are median-smoothed, so a one-day glitch can't fake a 7d/30d trend.

signal_glossary.volume_heat: Volume is large vs market cap (turnover ≥15%) — unusual interest building.
signal_glossary.vol_leads_price: Volume is hot but 7d price hasn't run yet — interest building BEFORE the move (the early sweet spot).

signal_glossary.low_float: Only a small share of supply circulates — CAUTION: unlock overhang can cap upside.
signal_glossary.tvl_surge: On-chain TVL jumped ≥25% in 7d from a small base — real capital arriving, not just token price.

pre_winner_lookalikes.method: validated winner-DNA coil screen (deep-below-high + oversold + at-30d-low [all validated, hold OOS] + below-ATH/high-vol/mid-float/small-cap); primed-but-not-yet-moved. NECESSARY-not-sufficient setup — needs an event trigger.
pre_winner_lookalikes.how_to_use: Beaten-down coils matching the data-validated winner DNA. SETUPS, not buys: most never move. Edge comes ONLY from confluence — a lookalike that is also trending / in a heating narrative / has a near catalyst / has fresh dev-gov.

signal_glossary.deep_below_60d_high: Trading <50% of its 60-day high — deeply beaten down. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.oversold_30d: Down >25% over 30 days — oversold. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.at_30d_low: Trading within ~3% of its 30-day low RIGHT NOW — the capitulation launch zone. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample); a bounce off the low actually LOWERS winner odds, so this is a timing edge.
signal_glossary.oversold_90d: Down >40% over 90 days — sustained downtrend (supporting context).
signal_glossary.deep_below_ath: Trading <15% of all-time high — far from prior peak, room to recover.
signal_glossary.high_vol: Elevated 30d volatility — capable of large moves.
signal_glossary.mid_float: Meaningful but not-fully-diluted float — the winner sweet spot.
signal_glossary.small_cap: Sub-$100M market cap — small enough to multiply.

dev_governance.note: Pre-announcement layer (early, low-crowd): GitHub releases/commit-activity + Snapshot governance for tracked protocols. A fresh_release or a pending 'launch/fund X' proposal precedes the marketing post. Each item carries release_notes / body (truncated) + a keyword dimension_hint (raw, NOT a verdict) — the FOLLOW-UP is to read these and judge what the change actually does and whether it improves the protocol at a fundamental level (consensus/scaling/security/economics/new capability) vs routine housekeeping. No composite score.

v2.10.2 brings WIT2 (BP-signed witness announcements with transitive relay), pipelined state root computation for block import (disabled by default), the sequence store / preconfirmation pipeline (disabled by default), and a set of p2p, sync and RPC hardening fixes. It also carries every fix shipped in `v2.10.1-hotfix` and `v2.10.1-hotfix2`.

No hardfork, no database schema change, no resync required.

## Highlights

- **WIT2 witness propagation** (#2208, #2416, #2417): block producers sign each witness announcement; peers verify and relay it without executing the block, and serve witnesses pre-import. Cuts multi-hop milestone-vote latency for stateless validators. Mixed WIT1/WIT2 meshes are supported.
- **Pipelined state root computation on import** (#2180, #2371): overlaps SRC of block N with execution of block N+1. Off by default, enable with `[pipeline] enable-import-src = true`.
- **Sequence store and preconfirmations** (#2373, #2419, #2388, #2423 and follow-ups): block producers can publish the block lifecycle to a sequence store, with preconfirmation RPCs (`eth_sendRawTransactionForPreconf`, `bor_getPreconfTransactionReceipt`, `bor_getInvalidPreconfBlocks`). Off by default, enable with `[sequencer] enabled = true`.
- **P2P traffic control** (#2418, #2367): bounded per-peer reply queues and allowances, controlled tx rebroadcast, and dangling tx-fetch peers are retried instead of excluded forever.
- **Stateless verification self-heal** (#2401): detects and …[truncated]

#### Sui Protocol Version in this release: `138`

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27049: gas model changes, implementation related no user impact

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27943: On devnet and testnet at protocol 138, transaction effects no longer report transaction dependencies. The effects encoding retains an empty dependency vector; object versions and per-object previous-transaction metadata are unchanged.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28131: In protocol version 138, colliding deferred-transaction keys in the consensus handler merge their entries instead of overwriting, so re-deferred transactions can no longer displace previously deferred ones.

## Overview

> [!NOTE]
> This is an optional release for op-supernode operators. It contains stricter validation of hardfork activation times in rollup configs.

## Other changes


### Configuration

- op-supernode now refuses to load a virtual node's rollup config that activates two hardforks at the same timestamp after genesis. The check applies to Jovian and every later fork, and every fork is now checked for correct activation order. Forks that activate at or before genesis may still share a timestamp. Existing chains in the superchain registry are unaffected. A custom config that schedules, say, Karst and another later fork at the same post-genesis timestamp must be corrected before upgrading (#22838)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/op-supernode/v1.0.2...op-supernode/v1.0.3
